findings.title: Denial cache keys omit the identity type
findings.body: This key is used for users, service accounts, anonymous identities, and render services, but includes only the parsed UID. For example, `anonymous:0` and `render:0` both have UID `0`; an anonymous denial for a dashboard can therefore be reused for a renderer check that should be allowed. Include the identity type in the key to prevent one principal's denial from blocking another principal for the cache TTL.

findings.title: Underscore-separated fields make denial keys ambiguous
findings.body: The name and parent folder are concatenated without escaping or length delimiters. For example, `(name="a_b", parent="c")` and `(name="a", parent="b_c")` produce the same key. Since resource and folder UIDs can contain underscores, a denial for one resource can incorrectly deny access to a different, permitted resource until the entry expires. Encode the fields unambiguously.
